articles.title: French PM Lecornu says ready to declare state of emergency 'if needed'
articles.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu on Monday warned that he was prepared to declare a state of emergency as authorities struggled to contain ongoing violence after looting affected thousands of businesses over the weekend. The unrest linked to a student protest movement comes months before France’s presidential election, raising concerns over public security and political stability.

articles.title: French shops demolished after weekend riots across the country
articles.description: Protests across France have sparked widespread looting and violence, leaving shopfronts demolished and thousands of euros’ worth of stock stolen. On Sunday, President Macron held an emergency meeting with senior government officials, warning that "those who looted will have to pay for the damage".

articles.title: Contre les violences du 17 octobre, les élus ont appelé à « faire bloc » lors des rassemblements devant les mairies

articles.title: Ukraine deploys drone to airlift wounded soldier in 'world-first' operation
articles.description: Ukraine has evacuated a wounded soldier from the front line using an aerial drone in what a Ukrainian army brigade has described as a world-first operation. articles.title: World Food Programme to end aid for half a million in Gaza due to funding shortfall
articles.description: The UN World Food Programme has warned that funding shortages will leave about 500,000 people in the Gaza Strip without critical food aid in a territory where two thirds of the population remains acutely food insecure. The WFP said it is reducing its monthly assistance from 1.6 million to 1.1 million people.

articles.description: Le secrétaire d’État américain Marco Rubio appelle Volodymyr Zelensky à se concentrer sur la fin de la guerre, tout en démentant toute interruption du partage de renseignements avec Kiev.

articles.title: France faces reckoning with public order policing after violent protest weekend
articles.description: France reeled Monday after a weekend of nationwide unrest sparked by mass protests against the rising cost of living and in support of high school students’ demands over education funding. In the violent clashes that erupted, law enforcement officers and protesters were wounded, public buildings were set ablaze and businesses were looted, raising significant questions about the French police's approach to public order.

articles.title: French far right seeks to capitalise on protests with calls for law and order
articles.description: In the wake of the weekend's violence, the political camps have been trading blame for the “chaos”. The riots have played into the hands of the far-right National Rally, which has been quick to capitalise on the anger and fears over law and order. FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell takes a look.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo suspendu 30 jours pour avoir quitté sans autorisation le stage de la sélection portugaise
articles.description: L’attaquant star avait claqué la porte du rassemblement de la Seleçao das Quinas le 30 septembre, à la veille d’un match de Ligue des nations face au Danemark à cause d’un conflit avec son sélectionneur.

articles.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : Kiev visée par de nouvelles frappes ; l’Ukraine affirme avoir neutralisé 243 drones et quatre missiles russes pendant la nuit

articles.title: Paris weekend riots raise concerns for tourism industry
articles.description: France announced partial curfews in Paris and other cities on Monday after weekend demonstrations over soaring prices degenerated into some of the worst street violence in recent years. Images of riots and looting in France over the weekend have been seen across the world and are worrying the country's tourism industry. Could the violence put off foreign tourists from visiting? FRANCE 24's Selina Sykes reports.

articles.title: Brazil's Lula, Bolsonaro clash in bitter debate ahead of election run-off
articles.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and right-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro traded personal attacks in a heated presidential debate on Sunday, a week before a closely contested run-off. The rivals accused each other of lying and corruption while clashing over the economy, security and healthcare ahead of the October 25 vote.

articles.title: Midterms 2026 : comment Barack Obama et les Clinton se mobilisent pour les démocrates

articles.title: Pourquoi l’Iran intensifie ses attaques dans le détroit d’Ormuz
articles.description: Après une accalmie relative durant l’été, les attaques iraniennes contre les navires se sont intensifiées et étendues dans le golfe Persique.
